usage.callShape: POST https://x402.orth.sh/openai/images/edits with JSON body {prompt, model, images:[{data,filename,contentType}]} — x402 paid, ~$0.08

inputExample.prompt: add a small red circle in the center

usage.outputShape: body.data[].b64_json (or body.data[].url) on success — OpenAI image-edit response shape { created, data: [...] }; errors at body.error.{message,type,param,code}
quirks: Registry/discovery inputSchema is WRONG: it lists a single 'image' string field. OpenAI rejects that: 'Unknown parameter: image. For application/json on /v1/images/edits, use images (array).'

The correct field is 'images' and it must be an ARRAY of FILE OBJECTS, not strings. A base64/data-URL string is rejected: 'Invalid type for images[0]: expected an object, but got a string instead.' Use images:[{data,filename,contentType}] (the _file object convention).

This is a thin passthrough proxy to OpenAI POST /v1/images/edits — body is forwarded as application/json. All validation errors come straight from OpenAI, so OpenAI's images.edits JSON-mode schema is the source of truth.
Payment is real and confirms on Base (got txHashes); a 400 still charges $0.08 because the proxy pays-then-forwards. Get the body shape right BEFORE paying.
'prompt' is required; 'model' (gpt-image-1 or dall-e-2), n, size, quality, user are optional.

QA stopped at 2 paid attempts ($0.16) per money-safety ceiling without landing a 2xx; the images:[{data,filename,contentType}] shape is inferred from the OpenAI error chain and should be confirmed on first live use.
usage.guide: POST https://x402.orth.sh/openai/images/edits as JSON with x402 payment (~$0.08/call on Base, no API key). Send {prompt, model, images:[{data, filename, contentType}]} where each images[] entry is a file object: data = base64 of the source image bytes, filename e.g. 'src.png', contentType e.g. 'image/png'. Do NOT use the 'image' field or a bare base64 string — both are rejected with HTTP 400 (and you still get charged). On success read the edited image from body.data[].b64_json (or body.data[].url). It is a passthrough to OpenAI /v1/images/edits, so OpenAI's image-edit JSON contract applies.
